bel1: Is your waist less than half your height? Calculate your waist-to-height ratio, compare it with the NICE cut-offs and learn how to measure your waist properly.
bel3: Is your waist less than half your height? This simple ratio shows whether fat is building up around your middle. NICE, the UK’s national health guidance body, advises adults with a body mass index under 35 to keep their waist to less than half their height. All you need is a tape measure: measure, then calculate below.

bel44: NICE recommends this ratio for adults with a body mass index (BMI) under 35. The same cut-offs can be used for men and women and for all ethnic backgrounds. The same cut-offs also apply to children and young people aged 5 and over.
bel45: My BMI is normal; should I still measure?
bel46: Yes. BMI shows excess weight but not where the fat is stored. Waist-to-height ratio is a practical estimate of fat around the middle. People from some ethnic backgrounds are more prone to storing fat around the middle, and their risk of weight-related conditions rises at a lower BMI.
bel47: My ratio is above 0.5; what should I do?
bel48: This is not a diagnosis, but it does show that your health risk is increased. The aim is to keep your waist to less than half your height. You can talk to a doctor or dietitian about your activity and eating habits and have values such as your blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol checked.
